title: Eval / Quality Monitoring Demo - Nimbus Retail
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked through the Eval / Quality Monitoring features in Console and Optimize: prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons, and how to run automated evals against their prompt suites. Customer is interested in detecting prompt regressions post-rollout and comparing model variants for cost vs quality tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: share security docs, pricing, and a POC plan with trial credentials; schedule POC kickoff.
next_steps: Samir to send pricing and POC SOW
Jordan to share guide: setting up prompt sets + evals in Console
Send trial credentials and sample eval spreadsheet
Schedule POC kickoff next week (Tara preferred)
Run baseline A/B on two model variants and share results

Jordan Lee - Share Console guide & eval template - 2025-05-11

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-09
Time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood CSM), Tara Singh (Nimbus Head of ML), Miguel Alvarez (Nimbus Platform Eng), Priya Rao (Nimbus PM), James O'Neill (Nimbus Data)

Summary (auto): quick demo of Redwood Console's Eval / Quality Monitoring; focus on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons.

00:00 - Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time. quick intros, we have jordan on the ses side and aisha for csm.
00:18 - Tara: hi, thanks. we just want to see how you detect regressions when we roll a newer model and how it compares automatically to our existing deployment. latency/cost tradeoff is big for us, also data residency.
00:34 - Samir: perfect, that's exactly what this walkthrough will cover. high level: console + optimize can manage prompt sets, run evals, raise regression alerts, and show A/B dashboards. jordan i'll hand over to you for the demo.
00:50 - Jordan: cool thanks. so opening the console here, if you go to "Evals" you'll see prompt sets; we import a prompt spreadsheet or connect to a repo. for nimbus you'd upload your canonical prompts and expected outputs, right?
01:10 - Tara: yep, we have about 2k core prompts across search/faq/checkout flows, but for initial POC we'll pick ~200 golden prompts.
01:26 - Jordan: sounds good. i'll show creating a prompt set and a baseline eval. first we select model variants — you can pick hosted variants or dedicated endpoints. one note: when we run evals we capture token counts and latency distributions so you can tie quality to cost.
01:44 - Miguel: quick Q: is the latency we're seeing from evals representative of production? like when we have long sequences or large embeddings?
01:52 - Jordan: mostly yes; we sample real seq lengths and we have quantization profiles per model that mimic production. not perfect but close; also we can run bench jobs on dedicated pools to mirror your infra. there's also a KV cache note, sometimes the transcript shows KV cash in our logs — it's KV cache (laughs).
02:10 - Priya: ha ok. so if a newer model's nudge causes a drop in our NPS metric or a correctness metric, can we get an immediate alert?
02:18 - Jordan: absolutely. you define regression alerts on metrics per prompt set — e.g., exact match rate, Rouge, custom scoring. alerts can fire when delta exceeds threshold (absolute or relative) and integrate with Slack/pager/ops.
02:34 - Samir: and those alerts are tied to runs; you can see the diff view — A/B comparison — that shows per-prompt diffs, aggregated histograms, and example failures.
02:48 - Tara: can we flag prompts with business-critical tags so we treat them differently?
02:52 - Jordan: yes tags and severity. you can also create acceptance gates so runs fail CI if a regression exceeds tolerance. we have a guide for CI integration.
03:06 - James: how do you handle flakiness? some of our prompts have high variance depending on context.
03:12 - Jordan: good Q — we support multiple runs and bootstrapped confidence intervals, and we surface high-variance prompts separately. Also you can set per-prompt tolerances or exclude unstable prompts from gate checks.
03:26 - Samir: demo time: i'm going to upload a sample prompt set (i'm using a demo csv). uploading... import shows columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output, tags, severity, metric.
03:46 - Jordan: once uploaded, run config: choose models (we'll pick redwood/gpt-2-open-quant and redwood/gpt-3-lite for demo), metric selection: edit distance + custom scorer. scheduling options: ad-hoc or nightly.
04:10 - Miguel: those model names look a bit off, are those your internal names vs upstream providers?
04:14 - Samir: yeah sometimes our catalog uses shorthand; console also shows vendor mapping — e.g., open models vs our tuned variants. transcription sometimes shows 'redwood' as 'redwood inference' or 'redwood-infer' in export, minor naming drift.
04:36 - Jordan: running the eval... you'll see a progress bar and per-prompt sampling. for A/B we choose baseline=old model, candidate=new model. once complete we render an A/B diff with per-prompt examples.
05:00 - 05:30 sample render pause (demo running)...
05:30 - Jordan: ok results are in: front-page shows aggregate delta: overall exact-match down 1.8%, fluency up 0.5, median latency increased 12ms. drill in...
05:48 - Tara: show me the example failures.
05:50 - Jordan: here, example 42: expected "Confirm your order" but candidate produced "Order confirmed" which fails exact match but may be acceptable; we label this as a heuristic false-positive.
06:08 - Samir: that's why we have custom scorers and fuzzy metrics; exact match is strict. for business-critical prompts we recommend custom scoring or human-in-the-loop review.
06:20 - Priya: can the system auto-suggest thresholds? we've been iterating manually and it's slow.
06:24 - Jordan: Optimize has suggestions: it analyses historical runs and recommends alert thresholds and which prompts to include in core gating. suggestions show expected alert frequency and false-positive rate.
06:38 - Miguel: on infra, if we run these evals at scale will it spin up dedicated GPUs? what's the cost look like?
06:44 - Samir: by default evals run on hosted capacity; for heavy benching we can route to your dedicated pool if you have Redwood Dedicated. costs are visible per-token and per-run, and Optimize can estimate run cost before you execute. we'll include sample pricing in the docs.
07:02 - Tara: ok, security — we need SOC 2 documentation, SSO/SAML support, and KMS integration for keys. also data residency in eu-west-1.
07:12 - Aisha: we have a security pack; we can share SOC 2 and ISO docs. we support SAML SSO and RBAC, and for Private deployments or Dedicated we can enable customer-managed KMS and VPC peering.
07:28 - Miguel: any audit logs for who ran evals and what prompt sets contain sensitive data?
07:34 - Jordan: yes audit logs include run id, user, start/end, artifacts; you can redact prompt text at rest or configure retention policies. logs are exportable to your SIEM.
07:46 - Samir: back to product: in the A/B panel you can sort by worst delta or by business severity. it helps prioritize fixes.
08:00 - Jordan: show the regression alert config: you can set alert to Slack channel, webhook, or create Jira ticket automatically with failed prompt examples.
08:12 - Priya: great, can we attach a screenshot/example to a ticket?
08:15 - Jordan: yep we attach diff snippets, model ids, run ids and a link back to console.
08:24 - Tara: timeline question: we want to run a POC in the next 2 weeks and if good, expand to dedicated route. how long to spin up Dedicated?
08:34 - Samir: Dedicated lead time depends on capacity and region; typically 2-6 weeks for reserved pools. for POC we recommend hosted trial to get evaluation metrics quickly, then migrate to Dedicated for production.
08:48 - Miguel: does the eval system account for prefix caching effects? some of our requests benefit from pre-warmed KV cache so production latency is lower than cold bench.
08:56 - Jordan: we can run bench jobs that simulate warmed KV cache; in the console bench settings toggle warm cache and batching profiles. note: sometimes transcripts and exports spell it 'KV cash' which is a minor ASR hiccup — internal note.
09:14 - Samir: let's demo CI gate integration quickly — you drop the run command into your CI, it returns non-zero on failed gate; Jenkins/GitHub actions are supported.
09:30 - James: curious about false positives from stochastic models — do you suggest seed control?
09:36 - Jordan: for deterministic comparison set sampling seeds and use temperature=0 or lower; we also recommend averaging multiple seeds for noisy tasks. we support multi-sample evals and aggregate metrics.
09:50 - 10:00 misc chatter / background noise
10:02 - Tara: for the A/B results, can we export a CSV of failing prompts so our tagging team can triage?
10:08 - Jordan: export to CSV or BigQuery; we also have a human review queue in the Console to assign reviewers.
10:18 - Priya: demo was helpful. can you show a quick view of the dashboard for longitudinal tracking?
10:22 - Jordan: sure, switching to "Quality Trends" — this shows weekly deltas, rolling averages, and alert events. you can annotate rollouts to correlate regressions with deployments.
10:40 - Samir: sales note: we'll include a POC SOW that outlines 200 prompts, nightly evals, CI gate on acceptance criteria, and a 4-week timeline.
11:00 - Tara: sounds good. a few more security clarifications: will logs with prompt text leave our region? we need EU-only retention for certain datasets.
11:14 - Aisha: we can set retention and region for logs, and for Private deployments you can keep everything on-prem. we'll send the details in the security pack.
11:30 - Miguel: question on RBAC — can we limit who can create gates vs who can view results?
11:36 - Jordan: yes role-based permissions: viewer, editor, admin, and custom roles.
11:44 - Tara: what's the onboarding effort for our ML team? we have two ML engineers and one infra person to support.
11:52 - Samir: for a POC we'll do a 2-hour onboarding + setup call, one dedicated SE hour/week for the POC, and a one-off run to establish baselines. total ~6-8 hours of Redwood engagement.
12:10 - Priya: great. any competitor differentiators we should call out?
12:14 - Samir: compared to vendors who only have simple pass/fail gates, Redwood ties evals to cost metrics, supports private deployments and dedicated pools, and has robust per-prompt tooling and CI gating.
12:34 - Tara: ok let's talk logistics — what do you need from us to get started?
12:38 - Samir: key things: canonical prompt CSV (~200 prompts), acceptance criteria per prompt or per flow, account for region constraints, and contact for infra to configure VPC if needed. we'll also request a crmid if you want us to attach to sales pipeline.
12:58 - Tara: we'll provide prompts and acceptance criteria by Tue.
13:04 - Samir: awesome. i'm going to recap next steps.
13:08 - Samir: recap: Samir send pricing & POC SOW; Jordan share Console guide and eval template; Aisha send security pack (SOC2, SAML, KMS notes); Tara to provide prompt set and criteria; Miguel to share VPC details if private demo needed. schedule POC kickoff for next week.
13:34 - Miguel: ok thanks everyone.
13:36 - Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional ASR errors, slight speaker mislabels on a couple lines.

Attachments/References: "Eval-template.csv" (demo), "Redwood-Security-Pack.pdf" (will be shared), pricing sheet (link in follow up).

End of transcript.
